body: Here are two of my favorite hues thus far. ### Deep Purple ```lua local hues = require("mini.hues") vim.g.colors_name = "minihues-purple" local opts = { accent = "azure", background = "#151025", foreground = "#c0c8cb", } hues.setup(opts) require("plugins.mini.hues").apply_custom_highlights(opts) ``` ### Olive ```lua local hues = require("mini.hues") vim.g.colors_name = "minihues-olive" local opts = { accent = "green", background = "#18271a", foreground = "#c2c9c3", } hues.setup(opts) require("plugins.mini.hues").apply_custom_highlights(opts) ``` ## Persisting random themes I sometimes generate a random hue that I really like—such as the olive one from above: ```lua local hues = require("mini.hues") math.randomseed(vim.loop.hrtime()) local base_colors = hues.gen_random_base_colors() local opts = { background = base_colors.background, foreground = base_colors.foreground, saturation = vim.o.background == "dark" and "medium" or "high", accent = "azure", } hues.setup(opts) require("plugins.mini.hues").apply_custom_highlights(opts) vim.g.colors_name = "minihues-myrandomhue" ``` When I find one that I like, I want to be able to persist it for future use, so I wrote an exporter that will generate a new colorscheme with my custom highlights as well as a matching wezterm colorscheme (because you are a monster if your terminal and neovim themes aren't in sync 😄 ). My exporter opens two buffers with the rendered themes in case I want to edit them before saving. Typically I want to change the accent color based on the hue. The wezterm config is specific to a [dynamic configuration selector](https://github.com/wez/wezterm/discussions/5435) I recently wrote for my own wezterm setup that allows me to dynamically fuzzy select fonts, colorschemes, etc ... ```lua local M = {} local H = {} M.export_minihues_theme = function() local ok, theme_name = pcall(vim.fn.input, { prompt = "Enter name for color scheme: minihues-", cancelreturn = false, }) if not ok or theme_name == false then return nil end local filename = "minihues-" .. theme_name local p = require("mini.hues").make_palette({}) H.render(H.minihues_path(filename), H.minihues_template, filename, vim.inspect(H.minihues_opts(p))) vim.cmd("split") local display_name = "MiniHues " .. theme_name:gsub("^%l", string.upper) H.render(H.wezterm_path(filename), H.wezterm_template, display_name, vim.inspect(H.wezterm_opts(p))) end H.wezterm_path = function(theme_name) local dir = os.getenv("WEZTERM_CONFIG_DIR") return string.format("%s/colorschemes/%s.lua", dir, theme_name) end H.minihues_path = function(theme_name) local dir = string.format("~/.config/%s/colors", os.getenv("NVIM_APPNAME") or "nvim") return string.format("%s/%s.lua", dir, theme_name) end H.render = function(filename, template, ...) local rendered = string.format(template, ...) vim.cmd(string.format("edit %s", filename)) vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, 0, -1, false, vim.split(rendered, "\n")) end H.minihues_template = [[local hues = require("mini.hues") vim.g.colors_name = "%s" local opts = %s hues.setup(opts) require("plugins.mini.hues").apply_custom_highlights(opts) ]] H.wezterm_template = [[local M = {} local name = "%s" M.init = function() return name end M.activate = function(config) config.color_schemes = config.color_schemes or {} config.color_schemes[name] = %s config.color_scheme = name end return M ]] H.minihues_opts = function(p) return { background = p.bg, foreground = p.fg, accent = "azure", } end H.wezterm_opts = function(p) return { foreground = p.fg, background = p.bg, cursor_bg = p.azure, cursor_fg = p.azure_bg, cursor_border = p.azure, selection_bg = p.bg_mid2, scrollbar_thumb = p.bg_mid, split = p.bg_mid2, ansi = { p.bg_mid, p.red, p.green, p.yellow, p.azure, p.purple, p.cyan, p.fg_mid2, }, brights = { p.bg_mid2, p.red, p.green, p.yellow, p.azure, p.purple, p.cyan, p.fg_mid, }, indexed = { [136] = p.orange }, compose_cursor = p.orange, copy_mode_active_highlight_bg = { Color = p.bg }, copy_mode_active_highlight_fg = { Color = p.fg_mid }, copy_mode_inactive_highlight_bg = { Color = p.green }, copy_mode_inactive_highlight_fg = { Color = p.bg }, quick_select_label_fg = { Color = p.bg }, quick_select_label_bg = { Color = p.orange }, quick_select_match_bg = { Color = p.bg_mid }, quick_select_match_fg = { Color = p.azure }, } end return M ```
bodyHTML:
Here are two of my favorite hues thus far.

Deep Purple

local hues = require("mini.hues")
vim.g.colors_name = "minihues-purple"
local opts = {
  accent = "azure",
  background = "#151025",
  foreground = "#c0c8cb",
}
hues.setup(opts)
require("plugins.mini.hues").apply_custom_highlights(opts)

Olive

local hues = require("mini.hues")
vim.g.colors_name = "minihues-olive"
local opts = {
  accent = "green",
  background = "#18271a",
  foreground = "#c2c9c3",
}
hues.setup(opts)
require("plugins.mini.hues").apply_custom_highlights(opts)

Persisting random themes

I sometimes generate a random hue that I really like—such as the olive one from above:

local hues = require("mini.hues")
math.randomseed(vim.loop.hrtime())
local base_colors = hues.gen_random_base_colors()
local opts = {
  background = base_colors.background,
  foreground = base_colors.foreground,
  saturation = vim.o.background == "dark" and "medium" or "high",
  accent = "azure",
}
hues.setup(opts)
require("plugins.mini.hues").apply_custom_highlights(opts)
vim.g.colors_name = "minihues-myrandomhue"

When I find one that I like, I want to be able to persist it for future use, so I wrote an exporter that will generate a new colorscheme with my custom highlights as well as a matching wezterm colorscheme (because you are a monster if your terminal and neovim themes aren't in sync 😄 ).

My exporter opens two buffers with the rendered themes in case I want to edit them before saving. Typically I want to change the accent color based on the hue. The wezterm config is specific to a dynamic configuration selector I recently wrote for my own wezterm setup that allows me to dynamically fuzzy select fonts, colorschemes, etc ...

local M = {}
local H = {}

M.export_minihues_theme = function()
  local ok, theme_name = pcall(vim.fn.input, {
    prompt = "Enter name for color scheme: minihues-",
    cancelreturn = false,
  })
  if not ok or theme_name == false then
    return nil
  end
  local filename = "minihues-" .. theme_name
  local p = require("mini.hues").make_palette({})
  H.render(H.minihues_path(filename), H.minihues_template, filename, vim.inspect(H.minihues_opts(p)))
  vim.cmd("split")
  local display_name = "MiniHues " .. theme_name:gsub("^%l", string.upper)
  H.render(H.wezterm_path(filename), H.wezterm_template, display_name, vim.inspect(H.wezterm_opts(p)))
end

H.wezterm_path = function(theme_name)
  local dir = os.getenv("WEZTERM_CONFIG_DIR")
  return string.format("%s/colorschemes/%s.lua", dir, theme_name)
end

H.minihues_path = function(theme_name)
  local dir = string.format("~/.config/%s/colors", os.getenv("NVIM_APPNAME") or "nvim")
  return string.format("%s/%s.lua", dir, theme_name)
end

H.render = function(filename, template, ...)
  local rendered = string.format(template, ...)
  vim.cmd(string.format("edit %s", filename))
  vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, 0, -1, false, vim.split(rendered, "\n"))
end

H.minihues_template = [[local hues = require("mini.hues")
vim.g.colors_name = "%s"
local opts = %s
hues.setup(opts)
require("plugins.mini.hues").apply_custom_highlights(opts)
]]

H.wezterm_template = [[local M = {}
local name = "%s"

M.init = function()
  return name
end

M.activate = function(config)
  config.color_schemes = config.color_schemes or {}
  config.color_schemes[name] = %s
  config.color_scheme = name
end

return M
]]

H.minihues_opts = function(p)
  return {
    background = p.bg,
    foreground = p.fg,
    accent = "azure",
  }
end

H.wezterm_opts = function(p)
  return {
    foreground = p.fg,
    background = p.bg,
    cursor_bg = p.azure,
    cursor_fg = p.azure_bg,
    cursor_border = p.azure,
    selection_bg = p.bg_mid2,
    scrollbar_thumb = p.bg_mid,
    split = p.bg_mid2,
    ansi = {
      p.bg_mid,
      p.red,
      p.green,
      p.yellow,
      p.azure,
      p.purple,
      p.cyan,
      p.fg_mid2,
    },
    brights = {
      p.bg_mid2,
      p.red,
      p.green,
      p.yellow,
      p.azure,
      p.purple,
      p.cyan,
      p.fg_mid,
    },
    indexed = { [136] = p.orange },
    compose_cursor = p.orange,
    copy_mode_active_highlight_bg = { Color = p.bg },
    copy_mode_active_highlight_fg = { Color = p.fg_mid },
    copy_mode_inactive_highlight_bg = { Color = p.green },
    copy_mode_inactive_highlight_fg = { Color = p.bg },
    quick_select_label_fg = { Color = p.bg },
    quick_select_label_bg = { Color = p.orange },
    quick_select_match_bg = { Color = p.bg_mid },
    quick_select_match_fg = { Color = p.azure },
  }
end

return M

I love the way the purple looked, so I did some advertising for mini in [/r/vimporn](https://www.reddit.com/r/vimporn/comments/1d211kn/mininvim_configuration/) last night.
